children: TD Cowen analyst Lance Vitanza thinks Strategy could survive a crypto winter that lasts a full decade. His stress test is harsh: Bitcoin falls to $20,000 and stays there for up to ten years.

The catch is that Strategy may be one of the few still standing. Vitanza says many other Bitcoin treasury companies might not survive the same conditions, so the call reads less like a victory lap and more like a list of who might be left when it's over.

Vitanza's case rests mainly on liquidity. Strategy, formerly known as MicroStrategy and the largest public Bitcoin treasury company, has built US dollar reserves reported at between $1.4 billion and $2.19 billion.
That reserve is reported to cover more than 21 months of the company's obligations. In other words, Strategy can keep paying its bills for well over a year and a half without touching its Bitcoin.
Strategy's Bitcoin stack is also very large. Reports from 2025 to 2026 put its holdings at between 640,000 and 848,000 Bitcoin, enough that a forced liquidation would move the market by itself.

Vitanza has not been purely bullish. He has cut his price targets on Strategy, with revisions tied to expectations about where Bitcoin trades, and those targets now sit in a range of roughly $97,500 to $109,000 for year-end 2026.
He has still kept a Buy rating on Strategy's shares. Lower targets with an unchanged rating suggest he expects less upside than before but still thinks the business model holds up under pressure.
Part of that view rests on how Strategy raises money. The company has issued preferred equity and common stock, using preferred share sales to fund more Bitcoin purchases and to build up liquidity.

The metric Vitanza focuses on is Bitcoin per share. Strategy has raised capital while still increasing the amount of Bitcoin backing each share, which separates it from firms that simply dilute shareholders to stay afloat.

Vitanza's broader argument is that the Bitcoin treasury sector may be entering a Darwinian phase. He expects only the strongest balance sheets to thrive, while weaker players face a real risk of collapse under prolonged stress.

Smaller treasury companies generally lack Strategy's financial footing. Without large dollar reserves or reliable access to capital markets, a long stretch of low Bitcoin prices could leave them with little choice except selling coins at a loss.

For investors, Vitanza's framework draws a sharp line between scale and survival. Strategy's liquidity, its large Bitcoin position, and its access to both preferred and common equity markets give it options that smaller rivals do not have.

There is also a market-wide risk. If smaller treasury companies sell Bitcoin in large numbers to meet obligations during a downturn, that could add selling pressure, which is exactly the situation Strategy's reserves are meant to keep it out of.
The numbers to watch are Strategy's cash reserves relative to its obligations, how quickly it issues preferred and common stock, and whether Bitcoin per share keeps rising.
The scenario also needs some perspective. Vitanza's $20,000-for-a-decade case is a stress test rather than a forecast, meant to show how the company holds up when nearly everything goes wrong.

title: TD Cowen's Vitanza says Strategy could outlast a decade-long crypto winter
